text: A man who is really diffident, timid, and bashful, be his merit what it will, never can push himself in the world; his despondency throws him into inaction; and the forward, the bustling, and the petulant, will always get the better of him.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CXXX, to his son, London, February 4, Old Style 1751
